title: Hardship Settlement Signing Window: Days Added Back for a Recent Hardship Hold
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Recent-Hold Allowance

The ended date of the qualifying hold recorded under Ridgeline's Hardship and Protective Holds — or the fact that the hold is still active — bears on the signing window when a consumer accepts a Hardship Settlement of its Settlement Agreements by electronic signature.

**Rule.** Where the account's qualifying hardship hold is still active or ended no more than 45 days before the acceptance date, the Hardship Settlement recent-hold allowance of 3 days is added back; where it ended more than 45 but no more than 120 days before the acceptance date, the recent-hold allowance is 1 day; a hold that ended earlier earns no recent-hold allowance.

| Qualifying hold | Days between its ended date and the acceptance date | Allowance added back |
|---|---|---|
| still active | — | 3 days |
| ended | 45 or fewer | 3 days |
| ended | 46 to 120 | 1 day |
| ended | more than 120 | none |

## Hypothetical boundary cases

- Ended exactly 45 days before acceptance: 3 days. Ended 46 days before: 1 day.
- Ended exactly 120 days before acceptance: 1 day. Ended 121 days before: none.
